title: UK regulator opens investigation into Meta's content-use terms
dek: The CMA is investigating whether Meta's commercial terms unfairly constrain publishers whose website content could be used for AI, without finding a breach.
whatHappened: On October 30, 2026, the UK Competition and Markets Authority opened a competition-law investigation into Meta's commercial terms for businesses.
The CMA says the terms could allow use of publishers' website content for Meta products, including AI features, without a choice over that use.
According to the regulator, Meta paused the revised terms on October 28 for industry consultation after earlier delaying their introduction.
The case will assess dominance and possible abuse; the CMA explicitly says no infringement has been established.
whyItMatters: Publishers relying on Meta for distribution face a potential trade-off between access to audiences and control over content reuse; that concern is what the regulator is investigating.
For AI developers, this examines how platform contracts acquire content permissions, not just whether a crawler respects a website preference.
The official case timetable schedules initial information gathering through January 2027, with dates subject to change. A launch announcement is not an enforcement outcome.
take: The important distinction is between agreeing to distribute content and being required to accept broader reuse as a condition of reaching customers.
If the investigation changes those contract terms, it could affect publishers' negotiating position, but neither dominance nor unlawful conduct should be assumed before the evidence is assessed.
openQuestions: Whether the CMA will pursue objections, accept changes or close the investigation remains unknown.
